Gepirone ER is a serotonergic agonist with selective activity at the 5HT1A receptor that is not part of an established pharmacologic class but is similar in action to buspirone.
Gepirone is a new molecular entity whose primary mechanism of action is as a moderate affinity agonist of the 5-HT1A receptor.

EXXUA is not approved for use in pediatric patients [see *Use in Specific Populations* (8.4)].

vote.text: A Psychopharmacological Drug Advisory Committee (PDAC) met December 1, 2015: of the 13-member committee, 9 did not agree the Applicant provided substantial evidence of effectiveness and 9 did not agree there was a favorable benefit-risk profile, though 11 members agreed safety was adequately characterized. No advisory committee was convened for the current resubmission.

summary.text: EXXUA (gepirone ER) is a new molecular entity approved under a traditional 505(b) NDA for MDD in adults. The original NDA was received October 1, 1999 and had a long history of non-approvals; substantial evidence of effectiveness (two positive short-term studies, 134001 and FK-GBE-007) was established through a dispute-resolution appeal granted March 16, 2016, and the NDA was resubmitted December 23, 2022. No accelerated approval, breakthrough, fast track, orphan, or priority-review designations are documented; postmarketing requirements include pregnancy studies, a lactation study, and a thorough QT/QTc study.
